This reference pairs familiar Stata commands with R code and notes on differences.

## Browse the chapters

Choose a subject below, or use the Stata and R indexes.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
contents <- file.path(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "..", "pkgdown",
  "stata-reference-generated", "contents-en.html"
)
knitr::asis_output(
  paste(readLines(contents, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
)
```

## Look it up from the console

With tidystata loaded, `findit()` searches the same catalogue. Use a bare command,
quote longer syntax, or supply variable names:

```r
findit(reg)
findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)")
findit(tab, sex, region)
```

R functions and English or Chinese questions also work. Append
`|> print(n = Inf)` to see all returned examples, notes and sources.
See [`findit()`](../reference/findit.html) for details.

## Adapt an example

Replace illustrative variable names with yours. `data` is your dataset;
`data1` and `data2` are merge inputs, and `fit` is a fitted model.

The R label names the main package. Load any packages needed for unqualified
calls; many data-preparation examples use `library(dplyr)`.
`findit()` does not load or install packages.

## About the notes {#example-labels}

**Differs from Stata** flags a difference in defaults, missing-value handling,
estimation or output; the note explains it. Other notes offer practical tips.

Execution checks test the R code, rather than numerical equivalence with Stata.
Check missing values, weights, factor reference levels, join rules and standard
errors before adapting an example. A search match does not imply support for
every option.
